summary: Verified the public Expo web preview on a 390x844 mobile viewport, admin login, admin overview, home rendering, and backend health/catalog context. Home and admin flows passed; an initial Explore assertion was unreliable because hidden/duplicate route text was present, although the Explore screen visibly rendered correctly in the captured screenshot.

issues: Order status chips are horizontally clipped at the right edge in the 390px viewport; the horizontal strip is scrollable, but the last option is only partially visible initially.

action_items: Add testID attributes to primary inputs/buttons/navigation controls to make automated regression coverage reliable instead of relying on duplicate visible text.
Consider making admin order status controls wrap or provide a clearer scroll affordance on narrow screens.
critical_code_review_comments: Frontend API configuration reads EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL/Expo extra backendUrl; confirm this is intentional because the stated contract names EXPO_BACKEND_URL.
Admin order status updates only the status field; the customer-facing timeline.done values are never updated, so order tracking can remain visually stale after an admin status change.
The UI has almost no testID attributes on interactive controls, increasing regression-test fragility and making hidden duplicate route elements easy to select accidentally.

success_rate.backend: 100% (context plus service checks; no new backend test file needed)
success_rate.frontend: 90% (home, account/admin login, overview and mobile overflow passed; Explore assertion selector was unreliable)

seed_data_creation: No seed data created by this testing pass.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use unique selectors or URL routes; visible Explore content was confirmed in the screenshot despite the first body-text assertion encountering duplicate/hidden route text. Admin credentials were read from /app/memory/test_credentials.md.
rca_of_issue: The Explore test selected a duplicate/hidden navigation text node and then asserted against body text while the route transition was still settling. This is a test-selector/timing weakness, not confirmed app failure. The admin status/timeline mismatch is a backend/frontend data-model issue: PATCH /api/admin/orders/{id} sets only status while timeline is persisted independently and never recalculated.
